newsitem.title: GREECE: TRYFON SAYS HE WAS VICTIM IN DELTA SCANDAL.
newsitem.headline: TRYFON SAYS HE WAS VICTIM IN DELTA SCANDAL.

text.p: Panagiotis Tryfon, fined 700 million drachmas by the capital market commission over the Delta Securities affair, said on Monday that he was a victim of the scandal as well and would seek justice in court.

"(The commission) is attempting to distort the truth and present me, the sole victim in this case, as the one responsible in order to cover up the responsibilities of those who created the scandal," he said in a statement sent by the law office of Alexandros Lykourezos.
On Friday, the commission slapped fines totalling 1.5 billion drachmas on Athens bourse member Delta Securities and three other individuals for manipulative trading on shares of Magrizos.
The commission's decision was based on the findings of an audit by three international auditing firms it had retained after the Delta scandal broke late last year.
"Mr. Tryfon headed a group of individuals who had numerous transactions on shares of Magrizos and Parnassos , totalling 8.0 billion drachmas," it said.

Their trades sought to manipulate the market in these shares in terms of pricing, demand and supply, the commission said, adding that Delta was actively involved in these trades and provided them with financing arrangements.

"I have confidence that the judicial system which is investigating the case will not be influenced by the decision of the capital market commission which is legally and substantively questionable," Tryfon said in the statement. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
